issue.title: Code Review and Test GitHub API Remaining Pull Requests
issue.body:
## Relation to issue #346 
The sentiment analysis notebooks (#346) depend on the Kaiaulu R scripts (#349) because those scripts handle downloading and parsing GitHub issues, PRs, and comments into structured CSVs. Without downloading and parsing steps, the classifier has no text data to analyze. A pipeline also eventually has to be established so that the sentiment analysis takes in those data.

## Project Description
The goal of this issue is to review open Pull Requests from prior contributors associated to GitHub API. 

- [x] In order to do so, the existing Kaiaulu master branch and GitHub functionality should be used to see if it is in working order. Namely, I should test the Docs GitHub Section and associated Notebook.

- [x] Subsequently, I should test what is pending for the added functionality for GitHub to be merged into the master branch (a code review request for @carlosparadis should be issued once I believe it is ready). 
   - [x] Evaluate PR #301 which provides an `/exec` interface to Kaiaulu's GitHub. Execs are used to call Kaiaulu functionality via command line. Exec scripts are the primary way to interface to other tools, such as the Kaiaulu React Austin is working on.
   - [ ] List here other PRs or issues associated to GitHub that are open.

issue.title: Add capability to construct sentiment graphs
issue.body:
In pages 15 and 16 of Haotian's thesis, the following capabilities are listed as present:

 * Removal of Automatically Generated Content:[46][1] We identified and removed system-generated content, such as system reports and auto-replies. This step was crucial to filter out irrelevant information that does not contribute to understanding the developers’ sentiments.

 * Elimination of Quoted Original Text:[7] In email replies, original messages are often quoted, leading to redundancy. We employed regular expressions to remove quoted text, focusing only on the new content added by the sender.

 *  Exclusion of Large Code Segments:[7][6] To maintain the focus on communication content, large segments of code were excluded from the dataset. We identified and removed code blockers, ensuring the dataset contained primarily conversational text.

The goal of this task is to look through 3 artifacts:

 - [ ] Haotian's thesis appendix
 - [ ] The diff repo containing all the changes relative to Kaiaulu (private repo)
 - [ ] The existing PR by Haotian and code included there 

To identify these and any other relevant capabilities among these 3 artifacts. We should confirm both that the 3 capabilities above are available in code form, and if anything else is available. 

The code is to be commited to #347

milestone.title: Integrate Sentiment Notebook to Kaiaulu Exec

issue.body: As part of the thesis done by Haotian using Kaiaulu, we want to integrate the pre-processing functions that export the comment data back in Kaiaulu. The sentiment classifier itself, as is done in Python and is a system of its own, will live in a separate repo: https://github.com/sailuh/sentiment_classifier ------ Referenced from https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/issues/346#issuecomment-3387514587 ## R/jira.R **parse_jira(jira_issue_comments_path)** - parses a folder of JIRA issue JSON files and returns a named list with two elements, issues and comments, where each element is a data.table containing the relevant issue or comment fields standardized for further processing. **parse_jira_replies_with_comment(data)** (To be replaced with parse_jira_replies()) - Called in parse_jira_replies_with_comment(parse_jira(jira_issue_comments_path)) - The currently defined parse_jira_replies() seems identical and can replace it in this call, since it combines issues and comments into one table with the required columns (reply_id, reply_subject, reply_body, etc.) for further cleaning and analysis. - Recommended to delete the defined function "parse_jira_replies_with_comment(data)" and replace where it's called with "parse_jira_replies()" ## R/github.R **parse_github_replies(github_issue_path)** - parses GitHub issues, pull requests, comments, and commits from JSON files, and puts them all into one table with columns like who wrote it, the message, and the subject so it’s ready to use. ## R/mail.R **parse_mbox(perceval_path, mbox_path)** - parses an mbox email archive using Perceval, extracts key fields like message ID, sender, recipients, subject, and body, and returns a standardized data.table with consistently renamed columns for further processing. ## R/sentiment_clean.R **clean_jira_data(data)** - Removes bot-generated messages and 'Hudson' from the JIRA dataset. **clean_mbox_data(data, if_clean_vote=FALSE)** (Rename: filter_irrelevant_mbox_messages()) - Removes automated or irrelevant entries from mbox email data such as system-generated messages, Jira or GitHub notifications, and optional vote-related messages. **clean_mbox_comment(data)** (Rename: remove_invalid_or_duplicate_mbox_comments()) - Removes duplicate rows and any comment whose reply_subject doesn’t match a real reply_id in the dataset. **process_mbox_data(data)** (Rename: clean_and_prepare_mbox_subjects()) - Cleans and standardizes mbox email reply subjects, handling encoding issues and removing common prefixes like "Re:". **create_if_comment_column(data)** (Rename: mark_and_uniquify_comments()) - Adds an if_comment column. It marks a row as a comment when its reply_id is different from its reply_subject, and gives each such comment a unique ID so they can be distinguished from each other ## Misc Note: I've given possible function renames but can still be subjected to change. Additionally, all 3 pre-processing functions located in the sentiment_classifier repo in [filter.py](https://github.com/sailuh/sentiment_classifier/pull/2/files#diff-416889f8bad02bdeeb81399a11737cc761a70bce32334210b6bf10d5bd70db96); remove_punctuation(), clean_text(), and remove_markdown_content() can be refactored and move into R/sentiment_clean.R in order to keep the python notebooks as machine-learning only, keeping in mind that perhaps not all 3 of the pre-processing may be necessary to be placed in Kaiaulu, or that the code blocks of each function can be refactored into some existing R/sentiment_clean.R functions. Can think about this more thoroughly in the future. In this visualization, there are 4 files currently located in Kaiaulu. Within those boxes, represents the the 9 user-defined function calls (not including Base R library function calls) that would be integrated into Kaiaulu + 3 of the pre-processing functions in filter.py located in the sentiment_classifier repo. (Note: Some functions mentioned like parse_jira already exists within the file, they are here for reference since they were also called in the provided notebook) ## Post-meeting issue specification for 10/24/25 @carlosparadis Refactor Kaiaulu’s data pipeline to eliminate .csv dependencies and establish consistent abstractions for Capabilities and Data. # Goals - Remove .csv dependencies (Call R exec functions via subprocess.run() in python notebook) - Kaiaulu exec should support filtered data export for each platform independently (GitHub, JIRA, Mail). - Column Mapping — Determine if the Python notebook needs a helper function in the api folder to rename and map columns so R output matches notebook expectations. (If R outputs y columns and the notebook expects x, map y → x using a Python “mapper” function.) - Refactor R filters — ensure single responsibility and consistent use of reply-table input/output. - Refactor Python filters — align with new reply-table abstractions and remove .csv assumptions. ## Post-meeting issue specification for 10/30/25 @carlosparadis - Create a new function in the api folder of the sentiment_classifier repo that maps certain columns of a reply table to columns that the python sentiment classifier notebook expects (Python notebook expects "Text" and "Polarity" columns) - clean_mbox_comment(), create_if_comment_column(), and process_mbox_data() from Haotian's version of Kaiaulu will not be refactored into Kaiaulu due to ambiguity on the reliance of removing/editing rows depending on the columns reply_id and reply_subject, also purpose deemed unnecessary for Kaiaulu. - Determine what columns in a reply table the soon-to-be refactored python functions into Kaiaulu will apply pre-processing cleaning to. - parse_mbox() currently does two things: parses mail and columns into a reply table. To seperate concerns, parse_mbox() will be modified to just parse, and parse_mbox_replies() will be created to map columns into a reply table (To follow the already established architecture of parse_jira(), parse_jira_replies() and parse_github(), parse_github_replies()) ## Post-meeting issue specification for 11/6/25 - Architecture 3 proposed to address the ping pong concern of Architecture 2. Architecture 3 discussed to be preferred over Architecture 2 due to Architecture 2 python notebooks "Train.ipynb" and "Test.ipynb" reliability of data to be exported from tokenize_statistics.ipynb will be lost if planned implementation for tokenize_statistics.ipynb goes through. - clean_text() in api/filter.py lines 43 and lines 46; ``` 43: text = re.sub(r"^(On[\s\S]*?notifications@github\.com\s*?wrote:\s*?)?(^(\>).*\s)*", '', text, flags=re.MULTILINE) 46: text = re.sub(r"```[a-z]*\n[\s\S]*?\n```", "", text) ``` discussed to be possibly refactored into their own R functions in Kaiaulu. - transform_text() discussed to be omitted from being refactored into Kaiaulu. - remove_markdown_content() to be looked into, decide purpose and how its implemented into Kaiaulu. - tokenize_text() to be looked into, decide purpose and how its implemented into Kaiaulu # Goals - Determine pros and cons of Architecture 2 and 3 and determine which to implement. - Refactor python functions. parses a folder of JIRA issue JSON files and returns a named list with two elements, issues and comments, where each element is a data.table containing the relevant issue or comment fields standardized for further processing. **parse_jira_replies_with_comment(data)** (To be replaced with parse_jira_replies()) - Called in parse_jira_replies_with_comment(parse_jira(jira_issue_comments_path)) - The currently defined parse_jira_replies() seems identical and can replace it in this call, since it combines issues and comments into one table with the required columns (reply_id, reply_subject, reply_body, etc.) for further cleaning and analysis. - Recommended to delete the defined function "parse_jira_replies_with_comment(data)" and replace where it's called with "parse_jira_replies()" ## R/github.R **parse_github_replies(github_issue_path)** - parses GitHub issues, pull requests, comments, and commits from JSON files, and puts them all into one table with columns like who wrote it, the message, and the subject so it’s ready to use. ## R/mail.R **parse_mbox(perceval_path, mbox_path)** - parses an mbox email archive using Perceval, extracts key fields like message ID, sender, recipients, subject, and body, and returns a standardized data.table with consistently renamed columns for further processing. ## R/sentiment_clean.R **clean_jira_data(data)** - Removes duplicate rows and any comment whose reply_subject doesn’t match a real reply_id in the dataset. **process_mbox_data(data)** (Rename: clean_and_prepare_mbox_subjects()) - Cleans and standardizes mbox email reply subjects, handling encoding issues and removing common prefixes like "Re:". **create_if_comment_column(data)** (Rename: mark_and_uniquify_comments()) - Adds an if_comment column. In pages 15 and 16 of Haotian's thesis, the following capabilities are listed as present:

 * Removal of Automatically Generated Content:[46][1] We identified and removed system-generated content, such as system reports and auto-replies. This step was crucial to filter out irrelevant information that does not contribute to understanding the developers’ sentiments.

 * Elimination of Quoted Original Text:[7] In email replies, original messages are often quoted, leading to redundancy. We employed regular expressions to remove quoted text, focusing only on the new content added by the sender.

 *  Exclusion of Large Code Segments:[7][6] To maintain the focus on communication content, large segments of code were excluded from the dataset. We identified and removed code blockers, ensuring the dataset contained primarily conversational text.

issue.body: ### 1. Purpose Extend an existing capability of retrieving Pull Request Information via the GitHub REST API. Currently, users are able to extract some from pull requests, however not all data points have been retrievable. There are multiple points of interest that may be a valuable asset to implement in order to capture the development process (process mining), is extracting formation from pull requests in GitHub. On GitHub, reviewers are able to add comments to lines of code by clicking a plus icon on the left hand side of the code. There, they may write critiques and comments and have the option of simply adding one single comment to that code, or continuing an entire review that consolidates multiple lines of code for the assignee to iterate over. Finishing a review can be done on the top right of the file review page. Users can now add comments to an entire review, approve the pull request in order to be merged, or request changes for the assignee to fix. ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1019d091-db72-409b-b18e-4d34211da462) Here, the lower portion shows the comment endpoint while the top is the review endpoint. Currently, the review endpoint is not implemented in Kaiaulu. The review endpoint (GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/reviews) is able to get the 'state' of the review, either APPROVED, COMMENTED, or CHANGES_REQUESTED. https://api.github.com/repos/sailuh/kaiaulu/pulls/295/reviews The review endpoint as noted here: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/reviews?apiVersion=2022-11-28#list-comments-for-a-pull-request-review List View: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/reviews Individual Review: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/reviews/{review_id}/comments For in-line code comments, the comments endpoint connected with the pull number is used. https://api.github.com/repos/sailuh/kaiaulu/pulls/295/comments GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/comments ### 2. Process We must implement the remaining endpoints to retrieve more data on pull requests from GitHub. Here are the endpoints we can pull from and those marked with a link, have already been implemented. ### Pull Requests • [List Pull Requests](https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/c69d152f043e7d1cfdee99cbca6a1f92f6532206/R/github.R#L751): [Docs](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/pulls?apiVersion=2022-11-28#list-pull-requests) • Specific Pull Request: [Docs](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/pulls?apiVersion=2022-11-28#get-a-pull-request) • List Commits on a Pull Request: [Docs](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/pulls?apiVersion=2022-11-28#list-commits-on-a-pull-request) • List Files on a Pull Request: [Docs](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/pulls?apiVersion=2022-11-28#list-pull-requests-files) • Check Merge Status of Pull Request: [Docs](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/pulls?apiVersion=2022-11-28#check-if-a-pull-request-has-been-merged) ### Review Comments • [List Review Comments in a Repository](https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/blob/c69d152f043e7d1cfdee99cbca6a1f92f6532206/R/github.R#L809): [Docs](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/comments?apiVersion=2022-11-28#list-review-comments-in-a-repository) • List Review Comments on a Pull Request: [Docs](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/comments?apiVersion=2022-11-28#list-review-comments-on-a-pull-request) ### Review Requests • Requested Reviewers for a Pull Request: [Docs](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/review-requests?apiVersion=2022-11-28#get-all-requested-reviewers-for-a-pull-request) ### Reviews • List Reviews for a Pull Request: [Docs](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/reviews?apiVersion=2022-11-28#list-reviews-for-a-pull-request) • List Comments for a Pull Request Review: [Docs](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/reviews?apiVersion=2022-11-28#list-comments-for-a-pull-request-review) ### 3. issue.body: ### 1. Purpose The objective of this issue is to implement a way to visualize GitHub event data retrieved by Kaiaulu using a process discovery algorithm. To achieve this goal, event data will be from Kaiaulu and process mining techniques will be applied to form a visual workflow. This will enhance the functionality of Kaiaulu, providing deeper insights into data and overall project dynamics. ## 2. Process Research existing functionality built into the [pm4py](https://github.com/process-intelligence-solutions/pm4py) library. Extend exec/github.R to allow exporting GitHub API event data. Commits will be added to PR [#301 ](https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/pull/301) instead of a new branch. Next, prepare data extracted from Github to a correct format for process mining analysis. Implement a process discover algorithm and apply it to the data. Finally, generate a workflow visualization that maps event data from Github. Additionally create a vignette to showcase the functionality. ## 3. Task List - [x] Modify R/github.R to include new API functions related to event data extraction. - [x] Extend exec/github.R to provide a CLI (Command-Line Interface) for exporting API event data - [x] Preprocess data for process mining analysis - [x] Implement process discovery algorithm from [pm4py](https://github.com/process-intelligence-solutions/pm4py) - [x] Generate workflow visualizations with graph-based representations - [x] Document and demonstrate new functionality within vignettes/github_api_showcase.Rmd - [x] Document implementation for future reference ## 4. issue.body: ### 1. Purpose The objective of this issue is to implement a way to visualize GitHub event data retrieved by Kaiaulu using a process discovery algorithm. To achieve this goal, event data will be from Kaiaulu and process mining techniques will be applied to form a visual workflow. This will enhance the functionality of Kaiaulu, providing deeper insights into data and overall project dynamics. ## 2. Process Research existing functionality built into the [pm4py](https://github.com/process-intelligence-solutions/pm4py) library. Extend exec/github.R to allow exporting GitHub API event data. Commits will be added to PR [#301 ](https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/pull/301) instead of a new branch. Next, prepare data extracted from Github to a correct format for process mining analysis. Implement a process discover algorithm and apply it to the data. Finally, generate a workflow visualization that maps event data from Github. Additionally create a vignette to showcase the functionality. ## 3. Task List - [x] Modify R/github.R to include new API functions related to event data extraction. - [x] Extend exec/github.R to provide a CLI (Command-Line Interface) for exporting API event data - [x] Preprocess data for process mining analysis - [x] Implement process discovery algorithm from [pm4py](https://github.com/process-intelligence-solutions/pm4py) - [x] Generate workflow visualizations with graph-based representations - [x] Document and demonstrate new functionality within vignettes/github_api_showcase.Rmd - [x] Document implementation for future reference ## 4. issue.body: As part of the thesis done by Haotian using Kaiaulu, we want to integrate the pre-processing functions that export the comment data back in Kaiaulu. The sentiment classifier itself, as is done in Python and is a system of its own, will live in a separate repo: https://github.com/sailuh/sentiment_classifier ------ Referenced from https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/issues/346#issuecomment-3387514587 ## R/jira.R **parse_jira(jira_issue_comments_path)** - parses a folder of JIRA issue JSON files and returns a named list with two elements, issues and comments, where each element is a data.table containing the relevant issue or comment fields standardized for further processing. **parse_jira_replies_with_comment(data)** (To be replaced with parse_jira_replies()) - Called in parse_jira_replies_with_comment(parse_jira(jira_issue_comments_path)) - The currently defined parse_jira_replies() seems identical and can replace it in this call, since it combines issues and comments into one table with the required columns (reply_id, reply_subject, reply_body, etc.) for further cleaning and analysis. - Recommended to delete the defined function "parse_jira_replies_with_comment(data)" and replace where it's called with "parse_jira_replies()" ## R/github.R **parse_github_replies(github_issue_path)** - parses GitHub issues, pull requests, comments, and commits from JSON files, and puts them all into one table with columns like who wrote it, the message, and the subject so it’s ready to use. ## R/mail.R **parse_mbox(perceval_path, mbox_path)** - parses an mbox email archive using Perceval, extracts key fields like message ID, sender, recipients, subject, and body, and returns a standardized data.table with consistently renamed columns for further processing. ## R/sentiment_clean.R **clean_jira_data(data)** - Removes bot-generated messages and 'Hudson' from the JIRA dataset. **clean_mbox_data(data, if_clean_vote=FALSE)** (Rename: filter_irrelevant_mbox_messages()) - Removes automated or irrelevant entries from mbox email data such as system-generated messages, Jira or GitHub notifications, and optional vote-related messages. **clean_mbox_comment(data)** (Rename: remove_invalid_or_duplicate_mbox_comments()) - Removes duplicate rows and any comment whose reply_subject doesn’t match a real reply_id in the dataset. **process_mbox_data(data)** (Rename: clean_and_prepare_mbox_subjects()) - Cleans and standardizes mbox email reply subjects, handling encoding issues and removing common prefixes like "Re:". **create_if_comment_column(data)** (Rename: mark_and_uniquify_comments()) - Adds an if_comment column. It marks a row as a comment when its reply_id is different from its reply_subject, and gives each such comment a unique ID so they can be distinguished from each other ## Misc Note: I've given possible function renames but can still be subjected to change. Additionally, all 3 pre-processing functions located in the sentiment_classifier repo in [filter.py](https://github.com/sailuh/sentiment_classifier/pull/2/files#diff-416889f8bad02bdeeb81399a11737cc761a70bce32334210b6bf10d5bd70db96); remove_punctuation(), clean_text(), and remove_markdown_content() can be refactored and move into R/sentiment_clean.R in order to keep the python notebooks as machine-learning only, keeping in mind that perhaps not all 3 of the pre-processing may be necessary to be placed in Kaiaulu, or that the code blocks of each function can be refactored into some existing R/sentiment_clean.R functions. Can think about this more thoroughly in the future. In this visualization, there are 4 files currently located in Kaiaulu. Within those boxes, represents the the 9 user-defined function calls (not including Base R library function calls) that would be integrated into Kaiaulu + 3 of the pre-processing functions in filter.py located in the sentiment_classifier repo. (Note: Some functions mentioned like parse_jira already exists within the file, they are here for reference since they were also called in the provided notebook) ## Post-meeting issue specification for 10/24/25 @carlosparadis Refactor Kaiaulu’s data pipeline to eliminate .csv dependencies and establish consistent abstractions for Capabilities and Data. # Goals - Remove .csv dependencies (Call R exec functions via subprocess.run() in python notebook) - Kaiaulu exec should support filtered data export for each platform independently (GitHub, JIRA, Mail). - Column Mapping — Determine if the Python notebook needs a helper function in the api folder to rename and map columns so R output matches notebook expectations. issue.body: ### 1. Purpose The objective of this issue is to implement a way to visualize GitHub event data retrieved by Kaiaulu using a process discovery algorithm. To achieve this goal, event data will be from Kaiaulu and process mining techniques will be applied to form a visual workflow. This will enhance the functionality of Kaiaulu, providing deeper insights into data and overall project dynamics. ## 2. Process Research existing functionality built into the [pm4py](https://github.com/process-intelligence-solutions/pm4py) library. Extend exec/github.R to allow exporting GitHub API event data. Commits will be added to PR [#301 ](https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/pull/301) instead of a new branch. Next, prepare data extracted from Github to a correct format for process mining analysis. Implement a process discover algorithm and apply it to the data. Finally, generate a workflow visualization that maps event data from Github. Additionally create a vignette to showcase the functionality. ## 3. Task List - [x] Modify R/github.R to include new API functions related to event data extraction. - [x] Extend exec/github.R to provide a CLI (Command-Line Interface) for exporting API event data - [x] Preprocess data for process mining analysis - [x] Implement process discovery algorithm from [pm4py](https://github.com/process-intelligence-solutions/pm4py) - [x] Generate workflow visualizations with graph-based representations - [x] Document and demonstrate new functionality within vignettes/github_api_showcase.Rmd - [x] Document implementation for future reference ## 4. issue.body: ### 1. Purpose Extend an existing capability of retrieving Pull Request Information via the GitHub REST API. Currently, users are able to extract some from pull requests, however not all data points have been retrievable. There are multiple points of interest that may be a valuable asset to implement in order to capture the development process (process mining), is extracting formation from pull requests in GitHub. On GitHub, reviewers are able to add comments to lines of code by clicking a plus icon on the left hand side of the code. There, they may write critiques and comments and have the option of simply adding one single comment to that code, or continuing an entire review that consolidates multiple lines of code for the assignee to iterate over. Finishing a review can be done on the top right of the file review page. Users can now add comments to an entire review, approve the pull request in order to be merged, or request changes for the assignee to fix. ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/1019d091-db72-409b-b18e-4d34211da462) Here, the lower portion shows the comment endpoint while the top is the review endpoint. Currently, the review endpoint is not implemented in Kaiaulu. The review endpoint (GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/reviews) is able to get the 'state' of the review, either APPROVED, COMMENTED, or CHANGES_REQUESTED. https://api.github.com/repos/sailuh/kaiaulu/pulls/295/reviews The review endpoint as noted here: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/pulls/reviews?apiVersion=2022-11-28#list-comments-for-a-pull-request-review List View: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/reviews Individual Review: GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/reviews/{review_id}/comments For in-line code comments, the comments endpoint connected with the pull number is used. https://api.github.com/repos/sailuh/kaiaulu/pulls/295/comments GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls/{pull_number}/comments ### 2. Process We must implement the remaining endpoints to retrieve more data on pull requests from GitHub. Task List Here are the endpoint task list objectives: - [x] Pull Request Review - [ ] Review Comments on a specific pull request - [x] List Pull Request Commits - [x] List Pull Request Files - [x] Check Pull Request Merge Status - [x] Requested Reviewers for a Pull Request - [x] Output data on a table for readability. - [ ] Document implementation for future reference.

issue.body: As part of the thesis done by Haotian using Kaiaulu, we want to integrate the pre-processing functions that export the comment data back in Kaiaulu. The sentiment classifier itself, as is done in Python and is a system of its own, will live in a separate repo: https://github.com/sailuh/sentiment_classifier ------ Referenced from https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/issues/346#issuecomment-3387514587 ## R/jira.R **parse_jira(jira_issue_comments_path)** - parses a folder of JIRA issue JSON files and returns a named list with two elements, issues and comments, where each element is a data.table containing the relevant issue or comment fields standardized for further processing. **parse_jira_replies_with_comment(data)** (To be replaced with parse_jira_replies()) - Called in parse_jira_replies_with_comment(parse_jira(jira_issue_comments_path)) - The currently defined parse_jira_replies() seems identical and can replace it in this call, since it combines issues and comments into one table with the required columns (reply_id, reply_subject, reply_body, etc.) for further cleaning and analysis. - Recommended to delete the defined function "parse_jira_replies_with_comment(data)" and replace where it's called with "parse_jira_replies()" ## R/github.R **parse_github_replies(github_issue_path)** - parses GitHub issues, pull requests, comments, and commits from JSON files, and puts them all into one table with columns like who wrote it, the message, and the subject so it’s ready to use. ## R/mail.R **parse_mbox(perceval_path, mbox_path)** - parses an mbox email archive using Perceval, extracts key fields like message ID, sender, recipients, subject, and body, and returns a standardized data.table with consistently renamed columns for further processing. ## R/sentiment_clean.R **clean_jira_data(data)** - Removes bot-generated messages and 'Hudson' from the JIRA dataset. **clean_mbox_data(data, if_clean_vote=FALSE)** (Rename: filter_irrelevant_mbox_messages()) - Removes automated or irrelevant entries from mbox email data such as system-generated messages, Jira or GitHub notifications, and optional vote-related messages. **clean_mbox_comment(data)** (Rename: remove_invalid_or_duplicate_mbox_comments()) - Removes duplicate rows and any comment whose reply_subject doesn’t match a real reply_id in the dataset. **process_mbox_data(data)** (Rename: clean_and_prepare_mbox_subjects()) - Cleans and standardizes mbox email reply subjects, handling encoding issues and removing common prefixes like "Re:". **create_if_comment_column(data)** (Rename: mark_and_uniquify_comments()) - Adds an if_comment column. It marks a row as a comment when its reply_id is different from its reply_subject, and gives each such comment a unique ID so they can be distinguished from each other ## Misc Note: I've given possible function renames but can still be subjected to change. Additionally, all 3 pre-processing functions located in the sentiment_classifier repo in [filter.py](https://github.com/sailuh/sentiment_classifier/pull/2/files#diff-416889f8bad02bdeeb81399a11737cc761a70bce32334210b6bf10d5bd70db96); remove_punctuation(), clean_text(), and remove_markdown_content() can be refactored and move into R/sentiment_clean.R in order to keep the python notebooks as machine-learning only, keeping in mind that perhaps not all 3 of the pre-processing may be necessary to be placed in Kaiaulu, or that the code blocks of each function can be refactored into some existing R/sentiment_clean.R functions. Can think about this more thoroughly in the future. In this visualization, there are 4 files currently located in Kaiaulu. Within those boxes, represents the the 9 user-defined function calls (not including Base R library function calls) that would be integrated into Kaiaulu + 3 of the pre-processing functions in filter.py located in the sentiment_classifier repo. (Note: Some functions mentioned like parse_jira already exists within the file, they are here for reference since they were also called in the provided notebook) ## Post-meeting issue specification for 10/24/25 @carlosparadis Refactor Kaiaulu’s data pipeline to eliminate .csv dependencies and establish consistent abstractions for Capabilities and Data. # Goals - Remove .csv dependencies (Call R exec functions via subprocess.run() in python notebook) - Kaiaulu exec should support filtered data export for each platform independently (GitHub, JIRA, Mail). - Column Mapping — Determine if the Python notebook needs a helper function in the api folder to rename and map columns so R output matches notebook expectations. (If R outputs y columns and the notebook expects x, map y → x using a Python “mapper” function.) - Refactor R filters — ensure single responsibility and consistent use of reply-table input/output. - Refactor Python filters — align with new reply-table abstractions and remove .csv assumptions. ## Post-meeting issue specification for 10/30/25 @carlosparadis - Create a new function in the api folder of the sentiment_classifier repo that maps certain columns of a reply table to columns that the python sentiment classifier notebook expects (Python notebook expects "Text" and "Polarity" columns) - clean_mbox_comment(), create_if_comment_column(), and process_mbox_data() from Haotian's version of Kaiaulu will not be refactored into Kaiaulu due to ambiguity on the reliance of removing/editing rows depending on the columns reply_id and reply_subject, also purpose deemed unnecessary for Kaiaulu. - Determine what columns in a reply table the soon-to-be refactored python functions into Kaiaulu will apply pre-processing cleaning to. - parse_mbox() currently does two things: parses mail and columns into a reply table. To seperate concerns, parse_mbox() will be modified to just parse, and parse_mbox_replies() will be created to map columns into a reply table (To follow the already established architecture of parse_jira(), parse_jira_replies() and parse_github(), parse_github_replies()) ## Post-meeting issue specification for 11/6/25 - Architecture 3 proposed to address the ping pong concern of Architecture 2. Architecture 3 discussed to be preferred over Architecture 2 due to Architecture 2 python notebooks "Train.ipynb" and "Test.ipynb" reliability of data to be exported from tokenize_statistics.ipynb will be lost if planned implementation for tokenize_statistics.ipynb goes through. - clean_text() in api/filter.py lines 43 and lines 46; ``` 43: text = re.sub(r"^(On[\s\S]*?notifications@github\.com\s*?wrote:\s*?)?(^(\>).*\s)*", '', text, flags=re.MULTILINE) 46: text = re.sub(r"```[a-z]*\n[\s\S]*?\n```", "", text) ``` discussed to be possibly refactored into their own R functions in Kaiaulu. - transform_text() discussed to be omitted from being refactored into Kaiaulu. - remove_markdown_content() to be looked into, decide purpose and how its implemented into Kaiaulu. - tokenize_text() to be looked into, decide purpose and how its implemented into Kaiaulu # Goals - Determine pros and cons of Architecture 2 and 3 and determine which to implement. - Refactor python functions. issue.body: ### 1. Purpose The objective of this issue is to implement a way to visualize GitHub event data retrieved by Kaiaulu using a process discovery algorithm. To achieve this goal, event data will be from Kaiaulu and process mining techniques will be applied to form a visual workflow. This will enhance the functionality of Kaiaulu, providing deeper insights into data and overall project dynamics. ## 2. Process Research existing functionality built into the [pm4py](https://github.com/process-intelligence-solutions/pm4py) library. Extend exec/github.R to allow exporting GitHub API event data. Commits will be added to PR [#301 ](https://github.com/sailuh/kaiaulu/pull/301) instead of a new branch. Next, prepare data extracted from Github to a correct format for process mining analysis. Implement a process discover algorithm and apply it to the data. Finally, generate a workflow visualization that maps event data from Github. Additionally create a vignette to showcase the functionality. ## 3. Task List - [x] Modify R/github.R to include new API functions related to event data extraction. - [x] Extend exec/github.R to provide a CLI (Command-Line Interface) for exporting API event data - [x] Preprocess data for process mining analysis - [x] Implement process discovery algorithm from [pm4py](https://github.com/process-intelligence-solutions/pm4py) - [x] Generate workflow visualizations with graph-based representations - [x] Document and demonstrate new functionality within vignettes/github_api_showcase.Rmd - [x] Document implementation for future reference ## 4. References - [Basics of Process Mining](https://www.ibm.com/think/topics/process-mining#:~:text=Process%20mining%20applies%20data%20science,and%20other%20areas%20for%20improvement.) - [pm4py importing csv files](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bWOKVx0PO6g) - [PM4Py python Publication](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S2665963823000933) - [Video with Core Ideas of PM](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XLHtvt36g6U&t=1181s) - [CLI Basics in R](https://cli.r-lib.org/articles/semantic-cli.html) ### Related Repo [sailuh/process_mining](https://github.com/sailuh/process_mining) ### Vision for the Feature
